messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are enforced; no “reasonable speed” exception.
• Speed limit signs are mandatory; if none, the default is 55 mph on highways, 35 mph on rural roads, 25 mph on residential streets. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop within 20 ft of a stopped school bus with flashing lights. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a stop sign, crosswalk, or intersection.
• Parking on a shoulder is allowed only when the vehicle is stopped. | | **Traffic Signals** | • Red means stop; green means go; yellow means prepare to stop.
• A flashing yellow light indicates caution. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing a vehicle requires a tow‑away permit if the vehicle is not in motion. | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Must display valid registration and proof of insurance. | | **Special Rules** | • “No‑stop” zones: vehicles must stop at all intersections.
• “No‑turn” zones: no left or right turns at specified intersections. | **Where to Find Official Texts** - Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 5) – the statutory source. - Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) – provides handbooks and updates. - Texas Highway Patrol – enforcement guidelines. **Common Enforcement Practices** - Speed cameras on major highways. - Random breath‑testing checkpoints. - School‑bus‑related stops. **Recent Updates (2023‑2024)** - 2023: Introduction of “no‑stop” zones in several counties. - 2024: Updated seat‑belt enforcement penalties; increased fines for cell‑phone violations. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to comply with a particular regulation!
